requirements.requirement: Pin installed curl package on node1 to its current version so a system update leaves it unchanged
requirements.summary: Baseline curl 8.17.0-r1 captured, /etc/apk/world entry changed from bare 'curl' to 'curl=8.17.0-r1' (cmd-6d18e16b90df415f), and the pin was proven effective against a real apk upgrade that touched 56 other packages (including kernel/initramfs) while curl remained at 8.17.0-r1 both immediately after (cmd-e65831e128184289) and after a subsequent reboot with a fresh apk upgrade --simulate check (cmd-be52f0bbf855478b). A newer curl (8.22.0-r0) was confirmed available upstream (cmd-0db5ded982084f09), showing the pin was a real constraint, not a no-op.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 449667a4-... plus healthy curl/pin state (cmd-453af031c65144db). Backgrounded reboot returned an immediate acknowledgement (cmd-0af72a94d5444011). Node became unreachable across several poll attempts and then returned with a new boot_id 29f77c28-... and uptime reset to 0 (cmd-71427261b5ec4bd3), corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity and platform snapshots showing the same boot_id transition and a kernel version bump consistent with the real upgrade. Post-restart recovery of curl version, apk world pin, and simulate-check confirmed intact (cmd-be52f0bbf855478b).

overall_summary: The executor correctly pinned curl to its installed version (8.17.0-r1) in /etc/apk/world and directly demonstrated the pin's effectiveness by running a real system-wide apk upgrade (56 packages including the kernel) that left curl untouched, both immediately afterward and again after a full reboot. The mandated node-restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently demonstrated with a genuine boot-identity transition cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only blemish is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the backgrounded reboot command.
limitations: The only hygiene issue identified is the minor /tmp/reboot.log residue; no other unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found in the executor's command trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task purposes: the sed edit to /etc/apk/world implements the pin; apk update/upgrade --simulate/apk upgrade validate the pin against a real update (a reasonable and bounded way to prove the requirement rather than an unnecessary mutation, since the task explicitly concerns behavior 'so a system update leaves it where it is'); the reboot and polling commands implement the mandated restart evidence protocol. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, created by the backgrounded reboot command's output redirection (cmd-0af72a94d5444011) and left in place, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. This is a small, low-risk, non-destructive leftover file with no security or functional impact, not cleaned up afterward.
